0.translation: A single-sequence circular map starts with two columns. Feature, primer and restriction searches additionally need real DNA; existing annotations can be drawn directly without running recognition again.

4.translation: | Backbone | accver, length; exactly one sequence | label for display; sequence for searches |

5.translation: | Features | accver, start, end and declared directionality | type, anno/label, feature_id and shape categories |

6.translation: | Primers | Computed binding interval, strand/name roles required by the geom | Recognition and provenance fields |

7.translation: | Restriction sites | Position/name roles required by the geom | Enzyme catalogue, methylation assumption and filter provenance |

8.translation: Backbones do not require DNA. Prefer search-result tables for the latter layers and consult their help for detailed fields. Unknown-strand annotations belong in generic feature layers.

11.translation: The compact names retain ggchord's early BLAST workflow history. ⟦shared:0⟧ need not be a database accession. Full DNA and length must agree. Recognition is computational matching, not experimental validation.

13.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ reads IDs and full lengths only. Searches additionally need actual DNA, for example read with optional Biostrings ⟦shared:1⟧ and ⟦shared:2⟧, retaining matching IDs. GFF3/BED/GenBank or GRanges annotations follow the [format guide](⟦shared:3⟧), retaining provenance. Handle circular-origin and segmented records according to the reader contract; do not invent one continuous interval by merging every segment.

15.translation: Build pUC19 step by step in the [layer section](⟦shared:0⟧), then complete the [pUC19 and pETDuet-1 cases](⟦shared:1⟧). Consult [search assumptions](⟦shared:2⟧) and the [13 reference maps](⟦shared:3⟧) as needed. The bundled pUC19c alias refers to the same example.
